iron.note: FR-4 tolerates heat well; the limit here is the component, not the board.

tools: Soldering iron with a fine tip, set to 350 °C
Flux — a pen or a small pot. Solder traces are not reliably makeable without it
A multimeter with a continuity buzzer (every checkpoint below uses it)
Hookup wire, AWG 24 in black, blue, orange, red, white, yellow — about 0.35 m in total
Tinned copper wire for the trace spines, 0.6 mm — about 51 mm (component lead offcuts do the job just as well)

phases.title: Preparation
phases.summary: Cut the board, mark hole A1, and get the iron and the parts ready.

phases.title: Lowest profile
phases.summary: Anything that lies flat: axial resistors and diodes. These go first because a board with a tall part on it will not sit flat on the bench, and a part that cannot be pressed down solders at an angle.

phases.title: IC sockets
phases.summary: IC sockets. The ICs themselves go in at the very end -- heat and static are the two things that kill them, and both are avoidable by fitting them last.

steps.span: B3 → E6, 8 pins with pin 1 at B3
steps.polarity: Pin 1 (the notched end, marked with a dot) in B3
notes: Fit a socket here if you have one — this phase is the sockets. The IC itself does not go in until the closing checks in phase 8, socket or no socket: it is the last thing on the board that should meet an iron.

phases.title: Small bodies
phases.summary: Small bodies: ceramic and film capacitors, TO-92 transistors, LEDs.

phases.title: Medium bodies
phases.summary: Medium bodies: electrolytics, TO-220 packages, crystals.

steps.polarity: Positive (long) lead in W3; Negative lead (the side with the printed stripe) in Y3
Positive (long) lead in B11; Negative lead (the side with the printed stripe) in D11

phases.title: Tall and mechanical
phases.summary: Tall and mechanical: connectors, terminals, potentiometers, switches, relays.

steps.span: W11 → Z11, 4 pins with pin 1 at W11

phases.title: Solder side: traces and bare wire
phases.summary: Turn the board over. Solder traces and bare wire, worked one net at a time so each is finished and checked before the next crosses it.

notes: Bare wire: it must not touch any other conductor along its length. Keep it flat against the board and check it against the neighbouring runs.
Lay the 0.6 mm tinned copper along the pads first and solder it at each one. Work in one direction and do not go back over a section that has cooled.
Tin each pad lightly first, then join them.
Flux is not optional on a run this long.

checkpoints.title: J1.1 ↔ R1.1
checkpoints.instruction: Probe J1 pin 1 and R1 pin 1.
checkpoints.expected: Continuous — they are both on net VCC.

checkpoints.title: R1.1 ↔ U1.8
checkpoints.instruction: Probe R1 pin 1 and U1 pin 8.
checkpoints.expected: Continuous — they are both on net VCC.

checkpoints.title: LED1.1 ↔ R3.2
checkpoints.instruction: Probe LED1 pin 1 and R3 pin 2.
checkpoints.expected: Continuous — they are both on net LED_A.

checkpoints.title: C2.1 ↔ U1.5
checkpoints.instruction: Probe C2 pin 1 and U1 pin 5.
checkpoints.expected: Continuous — they are both on net CTRL.

checkpoints.title: GND run T11 → D11, 21 pads must read as a dead short
checkpoints.instruction: Measure between T11 and D11, then touch the probes together and compare. A good run adds nothing you can read.
checkpoints.expected: The same as your probes touched together, give or take one count. This run should be about 2.7 mΩ, far below what a hand meter resolves — so any reading you can actually distinguish is a cold joint or a crack, not the copper.

phases.title: Long insulated wires
phases.summary: Insulated wire, which may cross anything already on the solder side.

checkpoints.title: R3.1 ↔ U1.3
checkpoints.instruction: Probe R3 pin 1 and U1 pin 3.
checkpoints.expected: Continuous — they are both on net OUT.

checkpoints.title: C1.2 ↔ C2.2
checkpoints.instruction: Probe C1 pin 2 and C2 pin 2.
checkpoints.expected: Continuous — they are both on net GND.

checkpoints.title: C2.2 ↔ J1.2
checkpoints.instruction: Probe C2 pin 2 and J1 pin 2.
checkpoints.expected: Continuous — they are both on net GND.

checkpoints.title: J1.2 ↔ LED1.2
checkpoints.instruction: Probe J1 pin 2 and LED1 pin 2.
checkpoints.expected: Continuous — they are both on net GND.

checkpoints.title: LED1.2 ↔ U1.1
checkpoints.instruction: Probe LED1 pin 2 and U1 pin 1.
checkpoints.expected: Continuous — they are both on net GND.

checkpoints.title: C1.1 ↔ R2.2
checkpoints.instruction: Probe C1 pin 1 and R2 pin 2.
checkpoints.expected: Continuous — they are both on net THRESH.

checkpoints.title: R2.2 ↔ U1.2
checkpoints.instruction: Probe R2 pin 2 and U1 pin 2.
checkpoints.expected: Continuous — they are both on net THRESH.

checkpoints.title: U1.2 ↔ U1.6
checkpoints.instruction: Probe U1 pin 2 and U1 pin 6.

checkpoints.title: R1.2 ↔ R2.1

checkpoints.title: R2.1 ↔ U1.7
checkpoints.instruction: Probe R2 pin 1 and U1 pin 7.
checkpoints.expected: Continuous — they are both on net DISCH.

phases.title: Closing up
phases.summary: Fit the ICs, run the final checks, and power up under current limit.

checkpoints.title: VCC ↔ GND must be separate
checkpoints.instruction: Probe J1 pin 1 (VCC) and C1 pin 2 (GND).
checkpoints.expected: Open, or at least the circuit's own resistance — never a short.

checkpoints.title: Polarity sweep before power
checkpoints.instruction: Look at every polarised part once more and compare it against the component-side sheet: C1, C2.
checkpoints.expected: Every stripe, band and flat facing the way the sheet shows. A backwards electrolytic fails loudly and a backwards diode fails silently.

checkpoints.title: Fit the ICs, pin 1 as shown
checkpoints.instruction: Only now put U1 into its socket, or straight into the board if you did not fit one, notch to the end the sheet marks. Straighten the legs on a flat surface first.
checkpoints.expected: Every notch and dot pointing the same way as the sheet.

checkpoints.title: First power-up, current limited
checkpoints.instruction: Set the supply to the circuit's voltage and the current limit to a little above what you expect it to draw. Watch the current as it comes up, and keep a hand on the switch.
checkpoints.expected: Current settles at roughly what you expected. If it runs into the limit, power down at once and go back to the isolation checks — something is bridged.
